history.title: Help a Seed Grow

data.body:
**Due:** (your teacher will tell you)

A seed may look like a pebble, but a healthy seed contains a living young plant. With suitable conditions, it can begin to grow.

1. Read **The Quiet Life of a Seed**.
2. Learn the words in the **Glossary**, then win the **Matching** game.
3. Look at the **What a Plant Needs** chart.
4. Sort the cards in **Need or Not?**
5. Practise explaining with **Plant Frames**, then check yourself against the rubric.
6. Take the quiz — say each answer out loud first.
7. Lock the ideas in with **Remember What a Plant Needs** — study the example aid, then make one your own.
8. Finish with **Investigation: The Windowsill Test** — use what you learned on a real problem, and mark every guess as a guess.

Your goal this week: watch a real plant or seed and notice what it does. Plants are slow, but they are always working. 🌱

Picture panels: From seed to seedling; Parts, light, and water; Space, nutrients, and care; Food-making and continued growth. Use these alongside the activities.

history.title: The Quiet Life of a Seed
history.data:
## The Quiet Life of a Seed

Hold a bean seed. It looks still, but inside a healthy seed is a tiny living plant and stored food. The seed does not become alive when it sprouts. It was alive already!

When conditions are suitable, a seed begins to grow. This is called germination. It needs **water**, **oxygen**, and a suitable temperature. Different kinds of seeds need different conditions. Some need light to germinate; others can start in darkness.

A bean takes in water. A small **root** emerges and grows down. A shoot grows up. Thick seed leaves, called cotyledons, contain stored food that supports this early growth.

Roots hold the plant in place. They absorb water and dissolved mineral nutrients. Roots also need oxygen. If soil stays soaked, water fills spaces that could hold air, making it harder for roots to get oxygen.

As green **leaves** develop, they capture light energy. They use that energy to make sugars from water and a gas in the air called carbon dioxide. This food-making process is called photosynthesis. Light supplies energy; soil is not the plant's food.

Growing green plants need enough light, water, air, mineral nutrients, room to grow, and suitable temperatures. **Sunlight** provides light outdoors and near windows. Special lamps can provide light too. More is not always better: too much water or too much heat can harm a plant.

During photosynthesis, a plant releases **oxygen**. Plants also use oxygen to release energy from their food. This happens during the day and at night, even when they are not making new food.

Watch a plant over several days. Draw its leaves, check the soil, and record what changes. If it droops, investigate before guessing why. A careful observer asks: What did I see? What conditions might explain it? What else could I check?

data.title: Remember What a Plant Needs
data.instructions: Two cards lock in the big facts from The Quiet Life of a Seed. Look at the example, make your own, and tell how it helps you remember.
data.sourceExcerpt: Seeds need water, oxygen, and a suitable temperature. Growing green plants also need light, mineral nutrients, and room. A bean root emerges before the shoot grows upward.

lessonRef.title: The Quiet Life of a Seed

cards.target: Conditions a growing green plant needs
essentialFacts: Seeds and plants need suitable temperatures.
Light powers food-making in green leaves.
Seeds and roots need oxygen; leaves use carbon dioxide.
Mineral nutrients and room support continued growth.
cards.aiExample: Water, air, light, and a suitable place: nutrients below and room to spread.
cards.mapping: The words name needs. Roots need room and nutrients. The plant also needs a suitable temperature. Each kind has its own needs.
cards.scaffoldStarter: My plant needs ____, ____, ____, and a place with ____.
scaffoldSteps: Check that your aid includes nutrients and space.
coachPrompts: Which word in your sentence is about the roots, not just the leaves?
cards.studentPrompt: Make a reminder of the conditions your growing plant needs.
cards.reasoningPrompt: Tell how each word helps you remember one need.

hookFact.text: A plant left in a dark closet will grow pale and weak, even with plenty of water, because it cannot make food in the dark.
hookFact.sourceTitle: The Quiet Life of a Seed (this lesson)

cards.target: First the root goes down, then the stem goes up
essentialFacts: When a seed wakes up, it sends a tiny root down into the soil.
The root absorbs water and anchors the plant.
Then a small green stem pushes up toward the light.
cards.aiExample: For a bean: root down, shoot up. Point down and then up to remember the directions.
cards.mapping: The two motions are the two directions, and doing 'down' first keeps the order right: the root comes before the stem.
scaffoldSteps: Point down and name the part.
Point up and name the part.
coachPrompts: What does the root do that the stem cannot?
cards.studentPrompt: Make your own down-then-up motion with words.
cards.reasoningPrompt: How does your motion help you remember which part grows first?

items.text: A seed needs ____, ____, and a suitable ____ to begin growing.
The ____ grows down to drink water and hold the plant still, and the ____ grows up toward the light.

data.rubric:
| Criteria | 1 — Starting | 3 — Getting There | 5 — Plant Scientist |
|---|---|---|---|
| Naming the need | Says the plant needs "stuff" | Names one or two plant needs | Names several needs, including nutrients and suitable temperature, and explains their roles |
| Plant words | Everyday words only | Uses 1-2 glossary words correctly | Uses 3+ glossary words correctly, including root and stem |
| Evidence from watching | No observation | One observation from a real plant | An observation with a day count and what it shows |

history.title: Plant Check

questions.question: Which of these is one thing a seed needs to begin growing?
Which part of a plant grows DOWN to drink water?
A plant is kept in a dark closet with plenty of water. What happens?
options: It grows faster in the dark because it is resting
It turns a brighter, healthier green in the dark
Nothing changes at all as long as it has water
It grows pale and weak because it cannot make food without light
questions.correctAnswer: It grows pale and weak because it cannot make food without light

questions.question: How does a green plant make food once its leaves develop?
options: It uses light to make sugar from water and carbon dioxide
It takes ready-made sugar from tiny stones in the soil
It gets all its food by taking in water through roots
It gets all its food from heat that warms its leaves
questions.correctAnswer: It uses light to make sugar from water and carbon dioxide

questions.question: What gas do green plants release while making food in light?
Name several things a growing green plant needs.
questions.expectedAnswer: Water, light, air, suitable temperatures, mineral nutrients, and room to grow.

questions.question: Your friend keeps a plant in a dark corner and waters it every day, but it is turning pale. What is missing, and why does it matter?
questions.expectedAnswer: The plant is missing sunlight. Plants use sunlight to make their own food, so even with plenty of water a plant in the dark cannot make food and grows pale and weak.

reflections.text: What is one plant you have seen this week? Where was it growing?
If you could grow any plant, what would it be, and how would you take care of it?

history.meta: 5 MCQ + 2 short answer • simple, read-aloud friendly

data.question: Can a plant get too much water? 💧
data.answer: Yes. Roots need air as well as water. Soil that stays soaked can leave too little air for roots. The plant may die. Each kind of plant needs the right amount of water.

data.question: Do plants sleep at night? 🌙
data.answer: Plants still work at night. Some leaves and flowers move. In the dark, green plants cannot use light to make food. They still use stored food and oxygen to get energy.

data.question: Why are leaves green? 🍃
data.answer: Many leaves have a green substance called chlorophyll. It takes in light that helps the plant make food. Some leaves have other colors that hide the green.

data.question: Can plants grow without soil?
data.answer: Yes. Roots can grow in water with nutrients mixed in. They also need oxygen and support. This way of growing is called hydroponics. Plain water alone cannot meet all these needs for long.

data.question: How do big trees start? 🌳
data.answer: An oak can start from an acorn. The seed holds a young plant and stored food. As it grows, it needs light, water, air, nutrients, room, the right warmth, and time.

data.question: Do plants really help me breathe?
data.answer: Yes. Plants and algae give off oxygen when they use light to make food. Many living things need that oxygen. Plants also use oxygen themselves, both day and night.

history.title: Investigation: The Windowsill Test
history.meta: 3rd Grade • Investigation brief • two cups, one change

data.title: The Windowsill Test
data.instructions: With your teacher, compare two similar young bean plants. Change one condition, predict what may happen, observe every day, and report what you actually find.
data.fitReason: Using established seedlings separates a test of growth in light from germination, which can begin using stored food.

brief.context: Your class has two young bean plants, or seedlings, of the same kind and size. They grow in matching pots with holes for water to drain. Use the same soil. Find two places with similar warmth but different light.
brief.audience: The class next door, who will see your cups and read your report
brief.drivingQuestion: What happens to these young plants when one gets less light?
brief.seedDirection: Change only ONE thing between your two cups. If you change two, you will not know which one mattered.
lockedLessonFacts: Seeds can begin growing using stored food.
Green leaves need light energy to make food.
Growing plants need water, air, nutrients, room, and suitable temperatures.
Roots need oxygen as well as water.
openQuestions: How can we change the light but keep other things the same?
What will we record besides height?
Could something else cause the changes we see?
criteria: Only one thing is different between the two cups
A guess is written down before the test starts
Something is measured or drawn every school day for a week
The report says what happened and uses at least two glossary words
constraints: Use young bean plants with your teacher
Watch for one week; some changes may take longer
Check how wet the soil is in the same way; give each plant the water it needs
After the test, put both plants where they can grow well
brief.deliverable: A picture journal with a drawing of both cups each day, your guess at the top, and two sentences at the end: what happened, and why.

parallelExample.context: A class compared two similar seedlings with different amounts of light.
parallelExample.move: They used matching pots and soil, kept temperatures similar, checked moisture in the same way, and recorded height, leaf color, and leaf number each day.
parallelExample.whyItHelps: They tried to vary only light and recorded several observations. Results are evidence to discuss, not a guaranteed outcome.

supports.frameStarter: We changed ____. We predicted ____. We observed ____. Another possible explanation is ____.
frameChoices: Compare brighter and dimmer light while keeping other conditions similar
coachPrompts: What else could differ besides light?
Did height, color, and leaf number tell the same story?
What can this short test tell us, and what remains uncertain?

data.coachHint: One change. Two cups. Look every day.
